item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q014_paper_example_reclassification_pa1492","answer":"In SCOP 1.69, PA1492 from PDB 1t1j was classified together with nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase from PDB 1f8y at a close homologous level, effectively treating PA1492 as part of the nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase family/superfamily relationship. Andreeva et al. 2008 used this as an example of a later correction: PA1492 was reclassified away from 1f8y so that the two proteins are no longer inferred to be close homologs and should not be used for direct functional transfer as nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferases. In the current SCOPe classification, their relationship is weaker: they may retain a broad structural resemblance at most, but PA1492 is not in the same SCOPe family/superfamily as 1f8y. Thus the practical change is from an over-specific homology/function/template assignment in SCOP 1.69 to a separated classification in current SCOPe, with PA1492 not a valid representative or close template for nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase function.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
